scope: Read-only P630 exact-output qualification/control review after 6ddfa1ac. Source and existing logs inspected; no builds/tests/native runs performed. Independent recommendation only.
disposition: Prior oracle sensitivity finding resolved for pinned P630 overlap case. All four targeted wrong graphs rejected in inspected negative-3 log; cohesive four-test batch remains pending as reported by parent. No new concrete flaw identified in this delta.

findings.status: resolved by source and existing negative-3 log inspection
findings.finding: PrematureResolve returned byte-identical output and assertion failed. Current changed-camera F-DOA case does not deliberately overlap partially covered suffix geometry with partially covered prefix edges; resolving samples early can be equivalent when suffix is disjoint or fully covered. Reduced-samples branch comes later and was not executed.
findings.required: Retain failure evidence. Add a bounded deterministic fractional prefix/suffix overlap case that distinguishes per-sample coverage, then complete remaining negative controls. This is oracle sensitivity failure, not demonstrated failure of correct prefix copy.
findings.resolution: Negative case now projects an actual F-DOA pad center through changed fractional camera and places a fractional full-viewport crosshair there; checks visible pad and nonempty suffix geometry. Existing negative-3 log reports 1 test passed, with differing channels stale335658, missing3061676, premature605, reduced4x50849; all three correct8x recovery comparisons exact. Prior insensitive control remains preserved in review_history and negative-2 log pin.

observations: Fault enum/module and injection branches are cfg(test), one-shot thread-local controls. MissingCopy deterministically clears B red, avoiding dependence on undefined discarded contents. StaleKey deliberately bypasses key matching; PrematureResolve resolves A to one pixel then expands it identically to 8 samples before original suffix.
Existing negative log rejects stale key (336044 differing channels) and missing copy (3062477 differing channels), with correct-graph recovery after each.

F-DOA log reports all 13 labeled cases and one test passed. Earlier combined small-fixture log reports terminal test passed but pointer/hover combined test failed due unsuitable no-pad fixture; preserve partial status.
Byte comparisons use the same current prepared snapshot and full shared painter, so they test graph/sample/order equivalence rather than independently validating scene preparation semantics.
Warm pointer cases assert zero world bundle execution and stable world upload identities/counters; these are useful mechanism checks, not timing/performance evidence.

Test recovery recreates renderer resources on the same device and transfers CPU session. It is not native device-loss, actual surface acquire/present, or replacement-device qualification; frame helper uses synthetic native receipt over offscreen capture.

Pinned fixture file currently matches manifest SHA256 7df67d426cc0cd808096824b0b7a05dcde351a1305fd41244d8c05a15801c08d. doa() itself only asserts pad count81; execution evidence must preserve supplied path/hash rather than treating pad count as identity proof.

The fractional crosshair-over-real-pad case makes partial suffix/prefix coverage observable without production mechanism changes. The 605-channel difference supports rejection of this premature-resolve graph, not universal sample-equivalence proof.
limitations: No performance trials or DRM duty qualification claimed.
Final native correctness coverage, fixture completeness and owner acceptance are outside these bounded source/log recommendations.

review_history.disposition: Positive comparisons support bounded graph-equivalence claims; premature-resolve oracle control remains failing, and reduced-sample control not reached in inspected run. Do not claim completed four-negative-control qualification.
